correctness.rationale: Every maximal geodesic in K_{n,n} minus a perfect matching is a length-three path a_i-b_j-a_k-b_i with pairwise distinct i,j,k. Omitted-index criterion U=empty OR |R|=1 OR |C|=1 OR R=C={i,h} is an exhaustive equivalence. Counting these sets by inclusion-exclusion yields T_n, removing chosen vertices classifies the three disjoint minimal families and M_n, and the explicit p=floor(n/2) vertex-disjoint length-three paths attain the vertex-count packing bound. Recomputed independent BFS maximal-path hitting sets for n=4,5,6 (24,60,120 maximal geodesics) and all 2^(2n) subsets; T_n and M_n agree exactly. This is finite corroboration of the unlimited-n combinatorial proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge original exact transversal and inclusion-minimal cardinality polynomials and packing ratio for crown graphs. The highly similar crown geodetic-set polynomial is an inequivalent coverage convention: it seeks S whose intervals cover all vertices, while this theorem hits every maximal shortest path. Earlier geodesic-transversal and packing papers establish the parameters and some other graph classes without the three-family crown enumeration. Full historical journal texts were not all accessible.
